source.title: Benign Loss Landscapes Can Coexist with Worst-Case Hardness
source.authors: Zach Furman; Stephan Wäldchen; Yang-Da Bei; Liam Hodgkinson

record.file_problem: Full text supplied; no apparent truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves loss-landscape results for tree tensor networks, a different model and theoretical method that bears on whether non-convex models with hard targets can have benign optimization landscapes. It does not test the listed CIFAR, initialization, shortcut, learning-rate, or normalization recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper's theorems, parity case study, and explicit spurious-minimum example are its own results relevant to the claim's loss-landscape subject. Cited results about other architectures are not extracted as rows. Statements that TTNs express hard targets and are polynomial-time evaluable do not report training outcomes.
record.test_reason: The study proves properties of tree tensor network population-loss landscapes. None of its results tests V1–V6. In particular, its spurious-minimum results do not measure gradient-descent outcomes or the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks required by V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors establish that TTNs contain worst-case hard-to-learn target families despite every minimum-norm local minimum being global, and prove a high-order parity saddle. They propose degenerate saddles as a mechanism for difficulty; they do not establish that these saddles cause slow SGD training, and explicitly note that degeneracy may be insufficient.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proves results about TTN squared-loss landscapes and gives a parity saddle case study; it does not run the benchmark training recipes in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Theorems depend on realizability, squared loss, tree topology, and (for the no-spurious-local-minimum result) minimum norm. The paper gives an explicit spurious local minimum when minimum norm is dropped.

fits_no_version.finding: For realizable TTNs with squared loss, every non-global critical point is Tucker-rank-deficient; every minimum-norm local minimum is global. Without minimum norm, non-increasing escape paths still exist, but spurious local minima can occur.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TTN population-loss landscapes can lack bad valleys and have only global minimum-norm local minima while permitting unrestricted spurious local minima.

fits_no_version.finding: The constructed halfway-learned parity point is critical with saddle order at least n/2. The study proposes degenerate saddles as a source of learning difficulty without proving training-time bounds for this point.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Realizable parity targets in TTNs can produce saddle points whose degeneracy grows with input size.

record.problems: The relevant evidence is theoretical and concerns a toy architecture, not benchmark classification training. The no-spurious-local-minimum result requires minimum norm, realizability, squared loss, and tree topology. The authors note the parity saddle-order bound may not be tight and that degenerate saddles may be necessary but not sufficient for optimization difficulty.

rows.subject: TTN (general tree tensor network)
rows.operation_detail: Proved that any critical point that is not a global minimum is rank-deficient.
rows.measure: Tucker rank at non-global critical points
rows.value: Any critical point of L which is not a global minimum is not full Tucker rank.
rows.note: The theorem is a structural statement about critical points, not a report of training-run outcomes or classification error.
rows.check: Accurately records Theorem 5.2, but Tucker-rank deficiency at TTN critical points cannot establish any listed version. This is a theorem, not an observed training outcome.

rows.subject: TTN (general tree tensor network)
rows.operation_detail: Proved global optimality of minimum-norm local minima.
rows.measure: Loss at local minima satisfying the minimum-norm condition
rows.value: Every local minimum of L that is a minimum-norm point is a global minimum with L = 0.
rows.note: This is a theorem with explicit assumptions; it does not establish convergence of a training algorithm from random initialization.
rows.check: Accurately records the conditional global-optimality theorem. Zero loss at minimum-norm local minima does not establish convergence from random initialization or any listed training effect.

rows.subject: TTN (general tree tensor network)
rows.operation_detail: Proved existence of a non-increasing-loss path from every non-optimal parameter point to a lower-loss point.
rows.measure: Existence of continuous path with non-increasing loss and strictly lower endpoint loss
rows.value: From any θ0 with T(θ0) ≠ T*, there exists a continuous path γ with non-increasing loss and L(γ(1)) < L(γ(0)).
rows.note: The authors explicitly state this does not rule out spurious local minima in unrestricted parameter space because the constant-loss path may leave any neighborhood.
rows.check: Accurately records existence of a non-increasing escape path. Such a path need not remain local or follow gradient descent, and measures none of V1–V6.

rows.subject: TTN parity case study, θ0
rows.size_stated: n inputs; n is a power of two and n ≥ 4
rows.operation_detail: Characterized the parity target's halfway-learned rank-1 parameter point as a high-order saddle.

conditions.value: parity on all n input bits
θ0 with every bond restricted to dimension 1 and every node tensor having uniform entries 1/2

rows.value: The point θ0 is a critical point of L, and a saddle of order at least n/2.
rows.note: This is a mathematical case study of a specified point, not an empirically observed training trajectory; authors say the bound may not be tight.
rows.check: The saddle-order bound concerns a constructed TTN parameter point, not measured training speed, trainable depth, or initialization comparisons. It bears on no listed version.

rows.subject: 3-leaf star TTN (Tucker decomposition), θ0
rows.size_stated: 3-leaf; core and leaf matrices are 3 × 3 × 3 and 3 × 3
rows.operation_detail: Constructed and proved a spurious local minimum without the minimum-norm assumption.

conditions.value: diagonal tensor T* = e000 + e111 + e222
bond dimensions equal target edge ranks, re = 3
θ0 specified in Appendix G.1; not minimum norm

rows.value: T(θ0) = T0 = e000 + e111; T0 − T* = −e222; L(θ0) = 1/2; θ0 is a local minimum and is spurious.
rows.note: The paper states the same output has a lower-norm parameterization: ∥θ′∥² = 8 < 14 = ∥θ0∥².
rows.check: The constructed TTN spurious minimum is correctly reported, but does not test V2's ReLU architecture, initialization outcomes, or width intervention. The loss 1/2 uses the appendix's unnormalized convention; the realizable global optimum has loss zero.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
